title: Stalks of the direct image of an abelian sheaf on a closed subspace
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $Z\subseteq X$ a closed subset with its subspace topology, $i:Z\to X$ the inclusion, and $F$ an abelian sheaf on $Z$ [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. Stalks $F_x$, germs and the induced stalk maps $\varphi_x$ of a morphism $\varphi$ are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], an abelian sheaf being a sheaf of modules over the constant presheaf of rings $\mathbb Z$. Define the abelian sheaf $i_*F$ by $(i_*F)(U)=F(U\cap Z)$ for open $U\subseteq X$. Then $(i_*F)_x=0$ for every $x\in X\setminus Z$, and for every $z\in Z$ the canonical germ map $(i_*F)_z\to F_z$ is a natural isomorphism of abelian groups, compatible with morphisms of abelian sheaves on $Z$.

proof.text: For an open V subset X, the definition gives (i_*F)(V)=F(V intersect Z), with restriction maps induced by restriction in F. Thus a germ of i_*F at x is represented by a section of F on V intersect Z, and a morphism of sheaves induces the corresponding map on these germ representatives.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 00AE, setup and definition of the direct image

proof.text: If x is not in Z, the open complement X\Z is a neighborhood of x and its intersection with Z is empty. Hence (i_*F)(X\Z)=F(empty)=0 for an abelian sheaf. Every germ at x restricts to this neighborhood, so the stalk (i_*F)_x is zero.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 00AE, proof: point outside the closed subset

proof.text: Fix z in Z. The neighborhoods V intersected with Z, as V ranges over open neighborhoods of z in X, are cofinal among the open neighborhoods of z in the subspace Z: if W is open in Z and contains z, write W=U intersect Z with U open in X and replace U by U union (X\Z). Conversely V intersect Z is a neighborhood of z. This is the neighborhood comparison used in the proof of Lemma 00AE.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 00AE, proof: every neighborhood in Z is Z intersected with an open neighborhood in X

proof.text: By this cofinality, the directed colimit defining (i_*F)_z is the same colimit as the one defining F_z. The canonical germ map sends the class of a section s in F(V intersect Z) to its class s_z, so it is well defined and bijective; equality is detected after restriction to a smaller neighborhood, and surjectivity and injectivity follow from the cofinal indexing systems.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 00AE, proof: stalk over a point of the closed subset

proof.text: The canonical map is an isomorphism of abelian groups because it is induced by the same section representatives and the germ maps preserve addition. For a morphism phi of abelian sheaves on Z, applying i_*phi to a representative s and then taking its germ agrees with first taking s_z and then applying phi_z; hence the isomorphisms are compatible with morphisms.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 00AE, abelian-sheaf clause and functoriality of germs
